metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the short term (1-3 days) after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is neutral or flat.
- Overestimates prices in the medium term (5-15 days) when recent prices are trending downward, suggesting lag in adjusting to mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike, model overshoots in the next 3-5 days, then gradually corrects — apply a 3-day decay factor to correct for momentum bias.
- When sentiment is flat (all 0.00), model should not assume strong directional bias; instead, anchor forecast to recent 7-day average or use conservative mean reversion.
- In the 15-30 day horizon, model tends to underestimate true price volatility — increase forecast by 5-10% if recent 18-day range is >10%.
- If true outcome shows a sharp reversal (e.g., 30d drop from 48 to 40), model should reduce forecast by 10-15% for next 5 days to account for momentum correction.
- When true outcome exceeds model forecast by >5% for 3 consecutive days, apply a “reversal bias” correction: reduce forecast by 2-3% per day until price stabilizes.
